summary: Confirmed DONE. a38ecac4b (on main and in the Hub-vendored 7bc39eec3) removes the second establishment. recoverHostedRelayConnection now only calls HostedHubController.connectionRecovered, which clears the relay gap, sets sessionEstablished:false and re-arms the session-sync deadline. It no longer calls retrySelectedNode, activateHostedNode, reset, disconnect or connect. The ordering checks out. relayEngine #applyModeLock flushes the buffered resubscriptions, emits online (which synchronously calls connectionRecovered), then emits sessionStatus 'synchronizing'. Hosted shell streams resubscribe without a resume cursor (service.ts resumeShell is false when hostedGeneration is set), so the replacement delivers a full snapshot that markHostedSessionReady accepts on the unchanged generation. The only remaining callers of retrySelectedNode are explicit ones: terminal-failure demand, browser resume, the draft retry and the UI retry button. Mobile's selected env is also adopted now. Before the fix it was released and rebuilt through nodeLifecycle.connectPrimaryEnvironment. The tests cover 2 tickets / 2 sockets per initial connect plus one drop, the stale-snapshot gap and the lost mutation. I found one small regression the auditor missed. The old path skipped recovery entirely (no rebuild, no deadline) while directoryStatus was not 'ready'. The new connectionRecovered arms the 30 s deadline unconditionally, so a directory that stays stale for more than 30 s after the relay returns now ends in terminal-failure.

evidence.note: recoverHostedRelayConnection is a one-liner calling hostedHubController.connectionRecovered(generation). The old queueMicrotask -> retrySelectedNode is gone.
On online with #recoveringAfterClose set, calls binding.connectionRecovered once per drop. The flag is set only on an unintentional close (line 521).

#applyModeLock: flush the buffered resubscriptions, then onTransportStatus('online') (connectionRecovered runs synchronously here), then onSessionStatus('synchronizing'), then onOpen. No inbound snapshot can reach markSessionReady before connectionRecovered has cleared the gap.
connectionRecovered: generation and gap fence, sessionEstablished:false, then #startSessionSyncTimer(generation) at :2636. It does not check directoryStatus or browserStatus.
markSessionReady ignores snapshots while #relayGapGeneration equals the current generation.

resumeShell is false for hosted. The shell resubscribes with a full snapshot. onResubscribe -> markHostedSessionReplaying (:868) and onCurrent/onReady -> markHostedSessionReady (:895-905) on the same hostedGeneration.

Before the fix, mobile's rebuild ran here: connectPrimaryEnvironment releases a non-ready connection and reconnects it, which created a new per-env record. Mobile now adopts instead (primaryConnection.ts:193 forwards to the shared controller only).

Adoption test: exactly 2 issueRelayTicket calls and 2 sockets across the initial connect plus one drop. retrySelectedNode, disconnectPrimaryEnvironment and connectPrimaryEnvironment are never called, and mutations are denied until markHostedSessionReady. :672 covers the gap snapshot and :701 the lost mutation.

A failed directory refresh sets directoryStatus 'stale' and effectiveRole null, with backoff up to 60 s (:2347). notifyDirectoryInvalidated is suppressed while #directoryRetry > 0 (:2169). Session-sync streams then get 'awaiting-session' (transport.ts:76-98, hostedRoleAllows with roleFresh=false).

#failSessionSync sets terminal-failure after HOSTED_SESSION_SYNC_DEADLINE_MS (30 s, :499). Before the fix, recoverHostedRelayConnection returned early on directoryStatus !== 'ready' (git show a38ecac4b^:packages/client-runtime/src/relay/transport.ts:260), and sessionEstablished stayed true, so no deadline applied in that case.

On web, a terminal-failure is retried only by the coordinator renewal tick or presence edge (comment at :358-361), and that retry is a full rebuild via retrySelectedNode. On mobile it needs a user retry or a lifecycle signal.

#invalidateAttempt (from onSessionStart/onDispose/reset) clears #recoveringAfterClose without clearing the controller's #relayGapGeneration. A WsTransport.reconnect() during a gap would leave the gap stuck (markSessionReady ignored, no deadline). This is latent only: hosted web disables generic reconnects (supervision.ts:1244, WebSocketConnectionSurface recoveryOwner), and on mobile the resume reconnect always follows suspendBrowser's generation bump.

fixDefects: 1) New terminal-failure path (low frequency, low to medium impact). HostedHubController.connectionRecovered (packages/client-runtime/src/authorization/state.ts:2624-2637) arms the 30 s session-sync deadline even when directoryStatus is not 'ready'. A stale directory nulls effectiveRole (state.ts:2342-2346), so the shell and the other session-sync streams stay 'awaiting-session' until the directory retry succeeds. That retry backs off up to 60 s, and invalidations are suppressed while it is backing off (state.ts:2169). After a Hub outage of roughly 60 s or more, the relay can recover more than 30 s before the next directory retry. #failSessionSync (state.ts:2810) then publishes terminal-failure with 'Ryco state could not be synchronized'. The pre-fix recoverHostedRelayConnection bailed out on a non-ready directory with no rebuild and no deadline, and sessionEstablished stayed true, so the session recovered by itself once the directory refreshed. Now web waits for the coordinator renewal tick and does a full rebuild; mobile waits for a user retry or a lifecycle event. 2) The auditor's mobile per-env note is accurate but minor. apps/mobile/src/connection/hostedConnectionCoordinator.ts connectionClosed (:503) and markSessionReady (:515) have no gap guard, and sessionEstablished is never reset on adoption, so reportShellSnapshotFailure (:538) is ignored there. The relay engine's 'synchronizing' on online resets the per-env sessionStatus, which neutralises most of the gap risk. Non-selected retained mobile connections always adopted like this, even before the fix. 3) Latent, not reachable today: #invalidateAttempt (transport.ts:604) clears #recoveringAfterClose but not #relayGapGeneration. Any future WsTransport.reconnect() on a hosted client during a gap would leave the session unable to become ready, with no deadline. Behaviour change, not a defect: the HostedReconnectPolicy backoff is no longer reset on every drop (the factory is not recreated), so flapping links back off progressively per the 60 s stable-interval policy.
implementationSketch: Defect 1: in HostedHubController.connectionRecovered (state.ts:2624), arm #startSessionSyncTimer only when directoryStatus === 'ready' and browserStatus is current or synchronizing. Otherwise record #deferredSessionSyncGeneration = generation. In the #refreshDirectory success branch (around state.ts:2294-2314, where directoryStatus becomes 'ready'), start the timer if the deferred generation equals the current generation and sessionEstablished is false, then clear the field. Also clear it wherever #relayGapGeneration is reset (around :1951) and on generation bumps. A simpler alternative: in #failSessionSync, re-arm instead of failing while directoryStatus !== 'ready'. Test in transport.test.ts: drop, set directoryStatus stale, replacement online, advance 30 s, expect transportStatus not terminal-failure; then set the directory ready and call markHostedSessionReady, expect ready; keep a test that the deadline still fires with a ready directory. Defect 2 (optional): give the mobile coordinator connectionRecovered(environmentId, generation), which clears a per-record gap flag (set in connectionClosed) and sets sessionEstablished:false. Have markSessionReady ignore snapshots while the flag is set, and call it from primaryConnection.ts:193 before forwarding. Cover it in hostedConnectionCoordinator.test.ts. Defect 3 (hardening): add an optional binding hook from #invalidateAttempt (or onSessionStart) that clears the controller gap for the current generation, or clear #relayGapGeneration in transportStatus('online') when no recovery is pending. Add a unit test that a reconnect() during a gap still lets markHostedSessionReady make the session ready.
decisionReason: The finding's fix is complete. The optional follow-up stays inside the authoritative hostedHubController and grants no authority: mutations still need the replacement's own accepted snapshot. It only restores the pre-fix behaviour of not timing out while the directory is stale. If maintainers prefer fail-closed-after-30s as the policy, they can keep the current behaviour.
correction: The auditor's DONE is correct. The auditor missed one regression: connectionRecovered arms the session-sync deadline without the old directoryStatus === 'ready' guard, so a directory stale for more than 30 s after relay recovery now ends in terminal-failure, where the old code recovered by itself. The mobile per-env gap issue is not purely new: retained non-selected mobile connections always adopted replacements this way. Only the selected env's record changed, from rebuild to adoption.
